newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan and Israel expand air links.
newsitem.headline: Jordan and Israel expand air links.

text.p: Jordan and Israel will expand air links and start a new Haifa-Amman route targeting Arab-Israeli passengers early next year, an airline official said on Tuesday.

"We have set a semi-final date of January 6 to launch our new once-a-week flight to Haifa," Ahed Qantar, head of Jordan's Royal Wings, a subsidiary of state carrier Royal Jordanian (RJ), told Reuters.
He said an extra sixth flight between Tel Aviv and Amman flown by Royal Wings would be launched on December 9.
The flights are in line with a joint transport accord agreed last January. Israel's mainly domestic carrier Arkia operates another five flights a week.
Under a clause of the accord, the two sides review traffic and discuss increasing the frequency of flights and passenger traffic on their air route every six months.

Officials said Jordan had proposed the Haifa-Amman route to cash in on the potential of the large Arab minority in Israel, predominantly in northern Israel around the Haifa area. Many have close family ties with Jordanians.
Arab-Israelis have crossed into Jordan in large numbers since a peace accord between the two countries in 1994 that ended a 46-year state of war.
Qantar said 14,000 Arab-Israelis crossed into Jordan by a northern land route in the last four months rather than head south to Tel Aviv and go by air.

Public and tourist buses and privately owned cars have started to cross the border, but Jordanians say bureaucratic hurdles under the pretext of security that delayed key cross border trade continue to hold back goods traffic flow.
